[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"ORM (Object-Relational Mapper) - SQLAlchemy in Python"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"SQLAlchemy is a powerful Python SQL toolkit and Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) that gives application developers the full power and flexibility of SQL. It provides a full suite of persistence patterns, all engineered for efficient and high-performing database access."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is an ORM?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"An Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) is a technique that lets you query and manipulate data from a database using an object-oriented paradigm. An ORM maps database tables to classes, and table rows to objects. This allows you to interact with your database using Python objects instead of writing raw SQL queries."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Why use SQLAlchemy?"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Abstraction: It abstracts away the differences between various database systems, allowing you to switch databases with minimal code changes."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Security: It helps prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities by automatically escaping user inputs."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Productivity: It increases developer productivity by allowing you to work with Python objects instead of writing SQL queries."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Maintainability: It makes your code more maintainable by separating the data access logic from the rest of your application."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Installation"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"To install SQLAlchemy, use pip:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"pip install sqlalchemy"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Basic Concepts"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Engine: Represents a connection to a database. It's the starting point for any SQLAlchemy application."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Session: Represents a 'holding zone' for all the objects you've loaded or plan to save. It provides a transactional interface."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Declarative Base: A base class for declarative class definitions. It allows you to define your database tables as Python classes."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Table: Represents a database table."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Column: Represents a column in a database table."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Relationship: Defines relationships between tables (e.g., one-to-many, many-to-many)."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: Defining a Model"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, String
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

# Define the database connection string
DATABASE_URL = "sqlite:///./test.db"

# Create an engine
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)

# Create a Session class
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)

# Define the base
Base = declarative_base()

# Define the model
class Item(Base):
    __tablename__ = "items"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    name = Column(String, index=True)
    description = Column(String, nullable=True)

# Create the tables in the database
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, we define an 'Item' model with 'id', 'name', and 'description' columns. The '__tablename__' attribute specifies the name of the table in the database. 'DATABASE_URL' specifies the connection string."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: CRUD Operations"},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

# Create a new item
def create_item(db: Session, name: str, description: str):
    db_item = Item(name=name, description=description)
    db.add(db_item)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item

# Read an item
def get_item(db: Session, item_id: int):
    return db.query(Item).filter(Item.id == item_id).first()

# Update an item
def update_item(db: Session, item_id: int, name: str = None, description: str = None):
    db_item = db.query(Item).filter(Item.id == item_id).first()
    if db_item:
        if name:
            db_item.name = name
        if description:
            db_item.description = description
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item

# Delete an item
def delete_item(db: Session, item_id: int):
    db_item = db.query(Item).filter(Item.id == item_id).first()
    if db_item:
        db.delete(db_item)
        db.commit()
        return True
    return False

# Example usage
db = SessionLocal()

# Create
new_item = create_item(db, name="Example Item", description="This is an example item.")
print(f"Created item: {new_item.name}")

# Read
retrieved_item = get_item(db, item_id=new_item.id)
print(f"Retrieved item: {retrieved_item.name}")

# Update
updated_item = update_item(db, item_id=new_item.id, name="Updated Item")
print(f"Updated item name: {updated_item.name}")

# Delete
delete_item(db, item_id=new_item.id)
print("Item deleted.")

db.close()"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"This example demonstrates how to perform basic CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations using SQLAlchemy.  It shows how to create a session, add objects to the session, commit changes to the database, and query for objects."},{"order":26,"type":"subheading","text":"Relationships"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"SQLAlchemy allows you to define relationships between tables using the 'relationship' function. This enables you to easily navigate and query related data."},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    name = Column(String)

    items = relationship("Item", back_populates="owner")

class Item(Base):
    __tablename__ = "items"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    name = Column(String, index=True)
    description = Column(String, nullable=True)
    owner_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"))

    owner = relationship("User", back_populates="items")"},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, a 'User' can have multiple 'Item's, and each 'Item' belongs to a 'User'. The 'relationship' function defines these relationships. The 'ForeignKey' establishes the link between the tables."},{"order":30,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"SQLAlchemy is a versatile and powerful ORM that simplifies database interactions in Python. It provides a high level of abstraction while still allowing you to leverage the full power of SQL. By using SQLAlchemy, you can write cleaner, more maintainable, and more secure code."}]
